question: How does the existing search compare with one-round action enumeration across the three example scenarios and several random streams?

one_round.candidate_sampling: Use the same eight starting sample seeds for every legal action at a decision. No tree or rollout policy.
one_round.value: Terminal result, otherwise the existing state heuristic.
one_round.tie_break: Stable card index, then target index, with pass first.

mcts.search_stream_scope: Reset per scenario, persistent across its five games.

work_accounting: Record one-round successor transitions and actual MCTS simulations separately. A MCTS simulation can advance several rounds, so these are not equal compute units. No efficiency claim.
limits: Protocol fixed before comparator outcomes are evaluated. No result-based tuning.
All seed/scenario cells remain, including losses.
Only five distinct environment seeds per scenario. Repeated search/policy seeds do not create independent environment samples.
The comparator has an independent decision algorithm but shares the simulator and heuristic. Neither is independent ground truth.
This bounded study does not establish general superiority or calibrated uncertainty.
